name: ice_storage_tank_discharge_phase_change
title: Ice storage tank discharge with phase change
summary: Discharge of a 120 m3 water/ice storage tank through a glycol heat exchanger over 50 000 s: the specific internal energy of the contents is integrated in time (INTEGRAL) and 5-argument IF logic tracks the ice fraction and the tank temperature through subcooled ice, melting at 0 C and liquid warming.

origin.course: Machines et systèmes thermiques (ULiège), repetition 6, exercise 4

verification.reference: EES stored solution of the sibling copy of the same exercise (thermo_models TM-0095, MSTH051024exercice4.EES: same physics, AU = 1 MW/K, P = 1 bar, complete 27-value stored solution); the runnable variant was re-run with those inputs and compared; closed-form check of the two discharge phases for the shipped inputs (the stored solution of TM-0104 itself is cleared: 16/40 values, inputs and constants only)
verification.notes: Variant (re-run with the TM-0095 inputs) vs EES: 19 common variables, 18 within 6.4e-8; printed maximum 5.23e-3 on u_dot (re-run at C-46) (excluded: final-time derivative ~1e-6 J/(kg s), proportional to 5-T_w ~ 4.3e-7, cancellation-limited); states agree to 2.5e-10 (u), 3.5e-10 (T_w, t_melt). Shipped inputs: trajectory matches the closed-form solution (melt complete at 30 460 s; final u 20 934.2 J/kg, T_w 4.9998 C).

related_external: CoolSolve examples/ice_storage_tank.eescode (CoolSolve transcription of the same exercise, CSX-023, kept in CoolSolve as a test case)
